questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.answer: The city/country of destination

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Met very nice people and made some friends. Had lots of issues with the renter (DUWO) and was not too excited about the experience of the university.

questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was through Vrije, so easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The conditions of the apartment that they rent, but this applies to both off and on campus, as they are all infamous for the uncleanliness and issues.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Just the proces of picking courses and than applying for them and enrolling in them. And picking up student card, which was all easy enough.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The student assistant team or what they are called were relatively helpful and available.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 10/10, got my classes

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I cannot think of anything right now.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My main courses had very few enrolled. The subjects were interesting, but one course in particular had very little engagement from the teacher, which was a shame.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Master's courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: One course was quite interactive with a very engaged teacher, the other was almost entirely uninteractive. So a mixed bag. My experience at UCPH consists of many more courses, so it's hard to make a general comparison, but I find courses to be pretty interactive and varied in teaching style. Also to have more students enrolled in them.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Neurophilosophy and psychiatry, Neuroethics and society and interdisciplinary research methods.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately, the programs of all these courses have been cut, so I would not recommend any of them.

Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's a shame they have this big nice social room with plenty of possible activites in it, including a grand piano, clay, kitchen area, board games and more., and it is closed off unless you have booked and appointment, which I find bizare and a total waste and shame.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: sports, events

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: volley in the nice weather

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: visit other dutch cities, explore amsterdam, take trains around europe.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are quite busy with their lives, my impression.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Non in particular.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How nice general strangers and people in the service industry seem to be.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find a nice location. DUWO has no issues with giving you a basically broken apartment that you have to spend time getting fixed yourself, so be prepared for that. Get the OV-chipkaart subscription.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of right now.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people and exploring towns.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The awful condition of my apartment upon moving in.

questions.answer: Yes
